For the unique largest binomial coefficient to occur at \(k=3\), we need
\[
\binom{n}{3}>\binom{n}{2}\quad\text{and}\quad \binom{n}{3}>\binom{n}{4}.
\]
From \(\binom{n}{3}/\binom{n}{2}=(n-2)/3>1\), we get \(n>5\).  
From \(\binom{n}{3}/\binom{n}{4}=4/(n-3)>1\), we get \(n<7\).  
Thus \(n=6\).

The general term is
\[
T_k=\binom{6}{k}(-1)^k2^k x^{(6-3k)/2}.
\]
For the constant term, \((6-3k)/2=0\), so \(k=2\). Hence
\[
T_2=\binom{6}{2}(-1)^2 2^2=15\cdot4=60.
\]

\[
\boxed{60}
\]
